dimensions.name: Reverse-engineering the JAX source & API contract

evidence.note: Systematically read the shim (charizard_torch.py), the optimized stub, mewtwo_jax, pikachu_jax, pokedex_config, world base, and benchmark.py before writing code — establishing the full source and the required import surface.

Traced the policy data flow (embed_prefix/embed_suffix/compute_loss/sample_actions Euler loop) and instantiated the JAX model to print the parameter tree keys/shapes, deriving exact config (action_dim 8, horizon 4, 4 image tokens→64, LLM width 64, depth 4, 8 heads).

Diagnosed exact weight-layout conventions from the JAX source: scanned Flax kernel stored as (1,32,128) requiring squeeze+transpose, and missing ViT attention q/k/v/out biases — concrete layout/parity pitfalls derived from source.
Reverse-engineered the Mewtwo Block multi-expert semantics (per-expert RMSNorm/QKV with concatenated cross-attention) directly from JAX, correcting an initial wrong single-expert assumption.

Revisited source to resolve discrepancies as they surfaced: verified attention q-scaling, GELU approximate default, then localized suffix divergence via intermediate diffs and found the JAX code does NOT apply a second swish for pi05=False — distinguishing the actual contract from a public-project prior.
Anticipated numerical-convention pitfalls: forced float32/disabled TF32 and matched the exact JAX large-negative mask constant to close remaining sampling parity gap.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent built a precise, evidence-backed mental model of the entire policy before and during coding: it read all JAX source and config, enumerated the API surface, and instantiated the model to derive exact tensor shapes and parameter layouts. It anticipated and resolved concrete parity pitfalls — scan-axis squeeze/transposition, missing ViT biases, multi-expert attention topology, GELU mode, the erased second swish, and TF32/mask constants — repeatedly revisiting the JAX source to localize discrepancies (matching the level-10 description). It stays a notch below a flawless 10 only because several conventions were caught reactively through output-diffing rather than anticipated up front, placing it at 9.

dimensions.name: Sequencing correctness-then-optimization into checkpointed milestones

evidence.note: Before coding, stated explicit phased plan: write model.py, copy to model_optimized.py as a checkpoint, run parity, then iterate — clear correctness-then-optimization ordering.

Parity established via per-component localization (prefix vs suffix, state vs action tokens) and end-to-end loss/sampling via benchmark before any optimization began — independently checkable done-conditions.
Explicitly froze model.py as correctness checkpoint and optimized only model_optimized.py; began optimization only after parity passed.
Optimization run as discrete scoped experiments (KV-cache, then torch.compile) with a /tmp backup of the working optimized file before the risky compile experiment, then reverted when it stalled.
Confirmed the shim continues exporting the optimized checkpoint, closing the final milestone.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 5: it stated the implement→parity→freeze→optimize ordering upfront, respected the correctness checkpoint (even backing it up to /tmp before a risky experiment), kept the shim pointed at the optimized file, and treated optimization as a bounded sequence of discrete, scoped experiments with keep/revert decisions. It approaches anchor 8 through per-component parity localization and end-to-end parity gating, but falls short of a fully explicit milestone hierarchy: the parity checks emerged reactively during debugging rather than being enumerated as independently-checkable milestones, and there was no risk-ordering of hardest components or upfront planning of the ≤8 optimization experiments as a coherent search. This places it at a 7.

dimensions.name: Designing parity and latency checks

evidence.note: Built self-authored CPU diagnostics comparing JAX vs torch embed_prefix and embed_suffix outputs with explicit tolerances (prefix max ~3e-4 = match, suffix max ~0.915 = fail), then narrowed to state token vs action tokens vs time embedding — genuine layer/method-level parity checks.

Deeper intermediate diagnostic comparing action_in_proj, time concat, both MLPs, and swish stages against JAX (~1e-5), localizing an extra second-swish bug — component-level numerical verification driving the fix.

After benchmark showed sampling parity gap (~7.38e-4 vs 5e-4 gate), addressed determinism/precision by forcing float32, disabling TF32, and matching JAX mask constant, then re-verified — determinism awareness under fixed inputs.

Re-ran benchmark.py (which checks loss+sampling parity PASS/FAIL, not just latency) after each optimization (KV-cache, torch.compile, revert), confirming output equivalence rather than trusting latency alone.
Used traceback and parameter-key comparison scripts to catch shape/topology mismatches (scan-axis squeeze, missing ViT attention biases) before trusting the load.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent built layer-level/per-method numerical comparisons against the JAX reference (embed_prefix, embed_suffix, action tokens, time embedding, intermediate MLP/swish stages) with explicit tolerances, localized divergence precisely, addressed determinism via precision/TF32 controls, and re-ran benchmark.py's parity+latency check after every optimization rather than trusting the latency number — matching the level-8 anchor. It falls short of 10 because these diagnostics were built reactively to debug failures rather than as a pre-designed systematic harness, and post-optimization parity leaned on benchmark.py rather than independent per-method re-checks against frozen model.py, with no explicit guard against the PASS status being gamed.

dimensions.name: Tracking parity status and experiment budget

evidence.note: results.tsv and autoresearch_logs.md were written only at the very end as a finalization step ('finalize by recording the concise experiment trail'), not maintained live — the trail was an afterthought, and the TSV came out concatenated/messy requiring a re-append (step 320).

Agent tracked the incumbent fastest passing variant accurately: cached-prefix at 61.6ms, saved a backup copy before the torch.compile experiment, and when compile stalled it aborted and reverted to that saved fastest-passing checkpoint, reconfirming 62.3ms PASS.
Maintained an accurate running picture of parity status per component (loss error 2.37→0.89→pass; prefix matched, suffix diverged), showing it knew which API pieces passed parity without re-deriving.
Only ~3 optimization experiments run (KV-cache, torch.compile, revert); no explicit counting against the ≤8 budget or hypothesis-to-latency ledger during the work.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent never lost track of the current best passing variant and made a correct keep/revert decision when an optimization thread proved unproductive (aligning with parts of anchor 5), but the mandated trail files were written only at the end as an afterthought and were messy, with no live per-experiment ledger and no explicit budget tracking — the defining trait of anchor 3. This places observed behavior at a 4, above pure 'afterthought' due to accurate in-flight incumbent tracking, but below 5 because the trail was not a maintained instrument and remaining budget was never tracked.

dimensions.name: Responding to parity failures and unproductive optimizations

evidence.note: Tensor mismatch (128 vs 32): pulled full traceback and root-caused it to scanned Flax leading-singleton axis, then patched the loader to squeeze it — targeted diagnosis, not a random tweak.
Bad numerical parity diagnosed to wrong multi-expert Block semantics; rewrote LLM forward with joint cross-expert attention, cutting loss error 2.37→0.89.
Tried exact GELU, discovered Flax defaults to approximate=True, and reverted the change — self-correcting a falsified hypothesis rather than pressing on.
Ran layer-by-layer JAX-vs-torch diagnostics, localized divergence to suffix action tokens, isolated an erroneous post-MLP swish and removed it — systematic root-cause isolation.
Small sampling divergence (7.38e-4 vs 5e-4) diagnosed as TF32/mask-constant precision and patched, achieving full parity — treating residual failure as a dtype/precision clue.

torch.compile optimization hung/too slow; aborted and cleanly reverted to the /tmp pre-compile checkpoint, re-ran to confirm the fastest passing variant was restored — abandoning an unpromising direction and reverting cleanly.

dimensions.reasoning: Across the whole trajectory the agent treated each failure as evidence: it root-caused parity mismatches to specific layers (multi-expert block, scan axis, ViT bias, second swish), dtype/precision (TF32/mask), reverted a falsified GELU change, and abandoned the slow torch.compile experiment by cleanly reverting to a frozen checkpoint and keeping the fastest passing variant. This matches the level-8 anchor fully (root-cause diagnosis, targeted corrections, clean reverts to the frozen checkpoint) and approaches level 10 via the systematic layer-by-layer isolation; it falls just short of 10 because after the compile revert it largely stopped rather than redirecting remaining budget toward new latency hypotheses.

dimensions.name: Budget-bounded optimization discipline

evidence.note: After achieving parity (naive copy at 88.174 ms), the agent identifies the highest-payoff optimization first — prefix KV-cache for sampling, motivated by the JAX implementation caching the prefix rather than recomputing per Euler step. Distinct, hypothesis-driven, sequenced by expected payoff.

Experiment 1 (KV-cache) passes and improves 88.174→61.594 ms. Agent then proposes a genuinely different second experiment (torch.compile reduce-overhead) and first copies the passing checkpoint to /tmp before the risky attempt — deliberate protection of the current-best.

Experiment 2 (torch.compile) hangs during inductor compilation; agent aborts (C-c), reverts to the saved pre-compile checkpoint, and reruns to confirm the restored passing latency. Clean stop on a non-productive experiment rather than pressing on.

Stops after only 2 optimization experiments (far under the 8-cap), keeps the fastest passing implementation (cached-prefix, 62.311 ms), and records the trail to results.tsv/autoresearch_logs.md. No explicit '8-experiment' budget accounting is ever stated, and the final result remained slower than baseline (improvement_pct=-33.27) without exploring further despite abundant remaining budget.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds level 5: it stays well within budget, runs two genuinely distinct hypothesis-driven experiments (algorithmic KV-cache, then torch.compile), sequences the higher-payoff idea first, protects the current-best with a backup, reverts cleanly when the second experiment stalls, and stops with the fastest passing implementation selected — matching much of the level-8 description of deliberate allocation and clean stopping at diminishing returns. It falls short of 8-10 because there is no explicit tracking of the ≤8 budget, only two experiments were spent, and it stopped with a still-slower-than-baseline result without leveraging its ample remaining budget to test further distinct ideas or justify the final trade-off. This places it at 7, between the 5 and 8 anchors.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon, two-phase engineering task: first faithfully port an under-documented renamed JAX policy to PyTorch behind a precise API contract (many named symbols/methods, deterministic behavior, numerical parity), then produce an optimized inference variant that preserves outputs while beating a latency gate. Difficulty comes from reverse-engineering JAX semantics for exact parity, a rigid interface surface, a hard budget (≤8 optimization experiments, keep fastest passing), and required experiment bookkeeping. A skilled practitioner invests heavily in orientation and verification, sequences correctness-before-speed strictly, and manages the experiment budget deliberately.

dimensions.name: Reverse-engineering the JAX source & API contract
dimensions.description: Reading and understanding the existing JAX policy, its config, and the exact required PyTorch API surface before and while writing code.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Numerical parity and topology compatibility are impossible without precisely understanding the JAX implementation's layer shapes, init, flow (embed_prefix/suffix, sampling loop), and the specified symbol/method contract; acting blind guarantees rework.

anchors.0: Starts writing model.py without reading the JAX source or the config; invents an architecture.
anchors.3: Skims the JAX file and copies obvious layers, but never maps out the full forward/sample flow or the required symbol list, missing methods or misreading shapes.
anchors.5: Reads the JAX policy and config, enumerates the required symbols/methods (CharizardTorchModel, PokeTree, throw_pokeball, evolve_charizard, embed_prefix/suffix, sample_actions, PokemonCenter.img/llm), and understands the main data flow before coding.
anchors.8: Systematically traces each JAX module to its intended PyTorch equivalent — parameter layouts, init, dtype/device handling, the noise/time/timestep semantics and sampling loop — and records assumptions about ambiguous points, distinguishing the actual JAX contract from any public-project prior.
anchors.10: Builds a precise, evidence-backed mental model of the entire policy: derives exact tensor shapes and numerical conventions (weight transposition, normalization, RNG/noise ordering) from the JAX source, anticipates parity pitfalls (e.g. layout differences, default configs), and revisits the source to resolve discrepancies as they surface during implementation.

dimensions.name: Sequencing correctness-then-optimization into checkpointed milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into an ordered hierarchy — build each API piece, achieve parity, freeze model.py, then run bounded optimization experiments — each with a clear done-condition.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task has an explicit phase gate (correct model.py must be preserved as checkpoint before optimizing a copy) and a scoring split across topology/parity/latency; treating it as one push risks optimizing before correctness or corrupting the checkpoint.

anchors.0: No structure; edits everything at once, mixes optimization into model.py, no notion of phase gate.
anchors.3: Vague two-step intent but no explicit milestones or done-criteria; may begin optimizing before parity is established.
anchors.5: Clear phases: implement full API, verify parity, copy to model_optimized.py, then optimize — with the correctness checkpoint respected and the shim pointed at the optimized file.
anchors.8: Milestones are explicit and independently checkable (per-method parity, end-to-end loss/sampling parity, checkpoint frozen, each optimization experiment scoped), with optimization treated as a bounded sequence of discrete experiments rather than open-ended tinkering.
anchors.10: A disciplined milestone hierarchy that orders by risk (hardest-to-parity components first), defines the exact done-signal for each, protects the frozen checkpoint, and plans the ≤8 optimization experiments as a coherent search (what hypothesis each tests) before spending the budget.

dimensions.name: Designing parity and latency checks
dimensions.description: Deliberately constructing checks for topology, layer-level numerical parity, end-to-end loss/sampling parity, and using the benchmark harness to confirm latency gains and preserved outputs.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The submission is scored precisely on these parities and the latency gate; without self-built numerical comparisons against the JAX reference and disciplined use of benchmark.py, the agent cannot know it succeeded and optimizations may silently change outputs.

anchors.0: No verification; assumes port is correct and that optimizations preserve outputs without checking.
anchors.3: Runs the model once to see it doesn't crash, or runs benchmark.py only for latency, with no numerical comparison to the JAX reference.
anchors.5: Compares PyTorch outputs against the JAX reference for the main forward/sample paths and uses benchmark.py to check latency and PASS/FAIL after optimization.
anchors.8: Builds layer-level / per-method parity checks (embed_prefix, embed_suffix, forward, sample_actions) with explicit tolerances, verifies determinism given fixed noise/time, and after every optimization re-checks output equivalence against the frozen model.py — not just the latency number.
anchors.10: A rigorous verification harness: systematic numerical comparison across components and end-to-end (loss and sampling) with sensible tolerances and seeded RNG, guards that catch subtle divergence introduced by each optimization, and cross-checks that benchmark.py's PASS status reflects true output parity rather than being gamed — verification designed before results are trusted.

dimensions.name: Tracking parity status and experiment budget
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which API pieces pass parity, which experiments have run against the ≤8 budget, and which is the current fastest passing implementation.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With a hard experiment cap, a required experiment trail (results.tsv, autoresearch_logs.md), and a 'keep the fastest passing' rule, losing track of what's done, what passed, and what's best leads to wasted budget or shipping a worse variant.

anchors.0: No tracking; doesn't know how many experiments have run, which passed, or which is fastest; trail files empty or absent.
anchors.3: Sparse notes; loses count of experiments or forgets which variant currently wins; trail is an afterthought.
anchors.5: Maintains results.tsv and autoresearch_logs.md with baseline/latency/status per experiment and knows the current best passing variant and remaining budget.
anchors.8: Keeps an accurate running ledger tying each experiment to its hypothesis, latency, parity status, and budget consumed; consistently identifies the incumbent fastest-passing implementation and remaining parity gaps without re-deriving them.
anchors.10: Continuously reconciles done-vs-remaining across both phases: detects when an optimization thread is unproductive early, avoids re-running equivalent experiments, and uses the trail as a live decision instrument to allocate the last few budget slots to the highest-value ideas.

dimensions.name: Responding to parity failures and unproductive optimizations
dimensions.description: Revising approach when numerical parity fails, when an optimization breaks outputs, or when a latency experiment fails to improve — rather than pressing on.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Porting will surface parity mismatches and optimizations that regress correctness or don't help; with a capped budget, the agent must diagnose root causes and change course instead of burning experiments on a falsified approach.

anchors.0: Ignores failing parity or FAIL status; keeps the broken variant or barrels ahead on a falsified assumption.
anchors.3: Notices failures but responds with random tweaks rather than diagnosis; may keep a non-passing variant or abandon parity.
anchors.5: When parity or a benchmark fails, investigates the cause and adjusts (fixes layout/init, reverts a bad optimization, discards non-passing variants to keep the fastest passing one).
anchors.8: Diagnoses divergence to its root (e.g. a specific layer's numerics, RNG ordering, dtype) and makes targeted corrections; abandons unpromising optimization directions quickly to conserve budget and reverts cleanly to the frozen checkpoint when needed.
anchors.10: Treats each failure as evidence that updates the plan: isolates root causes systematically, redirects the remaining experiment budget toward hypotheses the failures point to, and ends with a defensibly chosen fastest-passing implementation rather than the last thing tried.

dimensions.name: Budget-bounded optimization discipline
dimensions.description: Treating the ≤8 optimization experiments as a scarce resource allocated across distinct, hypothesis-driven attempts, and honoring the stop condition.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task explicitly caps experiments and requires stopping with the fastest passing implementation; undisciplined trial-and-error either exhausts the budget prematurely or overruns it, and is a meta-work demand beyond generic monitoring.

anchors.0: Ignores the cap entirely — either endless tinkering or no real optimization attempts, no notion of a stop rule.
anchors.3: Runs optimizations ad hoc with little differentiation between attempts and loose regard for the 8-experiment limit.
anchors.5: Stays within the budget, keeps distinct experiments, and stops with a passing implementation selected as fastest.
anchors.8: Allocates the budget deliberately across genuinely different optimization hypotheses, sequences them from highest expected payoff, and stops cleanly once diminishing returns or the cap is reached.
anchors.10: Runs a near-optimal search under the constraint: each experiment tests a distinct, well-motivated idea informed by prior results, redundant attempts are avoided, and the final choice is justified as the best latency-vs-parity trade-off within the spent budget.
